attributes.title: Level 4

subgroups.name: build 1

steps.hints:
❓ Did you change the sprite name in the [animate image] block and toggle loop to ON?

﻿
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja:

❓ What do you notice about the animated shark’s image? How does it give the appearance that it’s changing its movements?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡Follow this guide for directions on how to select an animation image:
steps.instructions:
Begin the project by animating the shark sprite!


Open the Animation code block menu and drag out an [animate image] block under the shark sprite’s position block. Select the shark sprite’s name.


Click the gray square next to the frames parameter, then open the Gallery tab. Select the sharkAttackRight animated shark sprite.


Change the interval parameter to adjust how fast or slow the animation runs. Toggle the loop parameter “ON” so the animation repeats continuously.


Click ▶ to see the shark sprite continuously open and close its mouth on the screen!

steps.hints:
❓ Did you match the sprite name in the [animate movement] block and toggle loop ON?

﻿
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja:

❓ Did you tinker with the movement and time parameters to select an effect and pace for how you’d like the orange fish to move?

❓What would happen if you kept the loop toggle set to off?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡Invite the ninja to test out different parameters for the [on game update every ms] and [animate movement] loops, and to try out different movement parameters for the sprite.
steps.instructions:
Animate a school of orange fish sprites!


Drag out an [on game update every ms] loop, and move the fish1 sprite’s blocks into the loop.


Open the Animation code block menu and drag out an [animate movement] block under the fish1 sprite’s position block. Select the fish1 sprite’s name.


In the movement parameter, click the dropdown to select a movement. In the time parameter, select the amount of time the animation should run for. Toggle the loop parameter “ON” if you want the movement to repeat continuously.


Click ▶ to test out different animated movements for the orange fish sprites.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you try out different animations in the movement parameter of fish2’s [animate movement] block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja:

❓ How did you choose what type of movement and time parameter to use for the white fish’s animation?

❓ What is different about the way you animated the fish sprites versus the shark sprite? 


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Encourage the ninja to think about how they’d like the white fish to move on the screen. Then, test out different movement parameters to find one that matches their vision.
steps.instructions:
Animate a school of white fish sprites!


Drag out another [on game update every ms] loop, and move the fish2 sprite’s blocks into the loop.


Open the Animation code block menu and drag out an [animate movement] block under the fish2 sprite’s position block. Select the fish2 sprite’s name, choose a movement parameter, time parameter, and toggle the loop parameter ON. 


Click ▶ to test out different animated movements for the white fish sprites.

steps.hints:
❓ Did you select a seaweed sprite from the Gallery, click the + button on the right panel, then select another seaweed sprite?

﻿
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution: 


Ask the ninja:

❓ What do you notice about the way you set up the shark sprite’s animation versus the seaweed? 

❓What other image could you add to the seaweed’s frames to extend its animation?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡Guide ninjas to notice how they can click on the play button to preview the animation.
steps.instructions:
Animate the seaweed!


Open the Animation code block menu and drag out an [animate image] block under the seaweed sprite’s position block. Select the seaweed sprite’s name.


Click the gray square next to the frames parameter, then open the Gallery tab. Since there are no animated seaweed sprites, create your own by selecting the 3 different seaweed images using the + button on the right. 


Change the interval parameter to adjust how fast or slow the animation runs. Toggle the loop parameter “ON” so the animation repeats continuously.


Click ▶ to see the seaweed sprite continuously move on the screen.

subgroups.introduction: Create a project that animates sprites in two different ways!

validationItems.text: The shark and seaweed sprites’ images are animated.
The orange and yellow fish sprites' movements are animated.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 4 of Yellow Belt! In this level, you’ll learn about using animation and music to make your projects even more awesome! Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 4:

badges.title: The Ol’ Razzle Dazzle
badges.description: Use animation and music to enhance a project.

badges.title: Saturday Morning Cartoons
badges.description: Use both image and movement animation in a project.

badges.title: On and On and On and...
badges.description: Repeat a melody or sound on loop in the background of a project.

badges.title: Original Score
badges.description: Compose a custom melody in MakeCode.
